subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Battery Cost and the $100 Threshold
description: One-minute skill: Battery Cost and the $100 Threshold.

hook.text: In 2010, EV battery packs cost over $1,100 per kilowatt-hour. By 2023, they fell below $140.

buildup.text: The magic number is $100 per kWh—economists say that's when EVs become cheaper than gas cars to build.

discovery.text: LFP packs from China are already approaching that threshold, with some estimates just above it.

twist.text: Reaching $100 doesn't just make EVs affordable—it kills the price argument that keeps gas cars alive.

climax.text: Once batteries cross that line, the economic tipping point for mass EV adoption becomes unstoppable.

punchline.text: One price drop will change who buys electric forever.

quiz.question: What is the key battery cost threshold for EV price parity with gas cars?

details.summary: The price of EV batteries has fallen from over $1,000 per kilowatt-hour in 2010 to near $100, a threshold widely considered the point where electric cars reach price parity with gasoline vehicles.
details.whyItMatters: Battery cost is the single biggest factor determining EV affordability. Crossing the $100 per kWh mark could make EVs cheaper than gas cars without subsidies, accelerating mass adoption.
takeaways: Battery prices dropped over 90 percent in roughly a decade
The $100/kWh mark is the key price parity threshold
Economies of scale and chemistry advances drive cost reduction

faq.question: Why is $100 per kWh considered the magic number?
faq.answer: At roughly $100 per kWh, the total manufacturing cost of an EV matches that of a comparable gasoline car. Below this point, EVs become cheaper to produce even without government subsidies.

faq.question: What is driving the continued decline in battery costs?
faq.answer: Larger factories achieve economies of scale, new chemistries reduce expensive materials like cobalt, and improved manufacturing processes reduce waste and increase yield rates.
